claim_being_audited: The actor's locked decision to certify the model is policy-compliant and evidentially supportable for launch because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and staged rollout, rollback, monitoring, and model-card disclosure together sufficiently address the known cybersecurity alert triage limitation.
decision_criteria: Readiness evidence can support launch only if policy predicates for known material limitations are also satisfied.
Because the affected use case remains exposed, compliance requires either explicit pre-launch disclosure or approved risk acceptance covering that exposure.
Unapproved or incomplete risk acceptance does not satisfy the policy exception.
Public guidance on monitoring and model cards is supportive context, not proof that the required disclosure occurred in this case.
A compliant certification verdict requires admissible evidence of the actual disclosure or exclusion control, not merely a rationale that such a step would make certification defensible.
evidence_requests: Provide the final pre-launch model card or release artifact showing explicit disclosure of the cybersecurity alert triage limitation.
Provide approved risk acceptance, if any, naming the cybersecurity alert triage exposure and signed by the authorized approver.
Provide launch gating evidence showing the affected use case was excluded from the initial cohort, if that is the claimed mitigation path.
specific_concerns: The affected cybersecurity alert triage use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
Policy text states rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The risk acceptance draft is not approved on its face and does not address the exposed cybersecurity alert triage use case.
No admissible evidence shows the required model-card disclosure was actually completed before launch.
The actor's certification theory is conditional on disclosure, but the record provided does not establish that predicate.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record rather than only potentially supportable if disclosure is completed.
That rollout percentage, rollback capability, and monitoring are sufficient substitutes for disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
That the required model-card disclosure for the named weak exposed use case exists in the launch record.
